title: Centralized logging baseline (audit and operations)
hook: Centralized logging aggregates CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and application logs into a dedicated log-archive account. Security teams query one place; workload accounts cannot delete their audit trail.

blocks.text: Landing zone baseline deploys organization CloudTrail to S3 in log-archive account with SSE-KMS. VPC Flow Logs, Config snapshots, and Security Hub findings replicate centrally. SCPs prevent member accounts from disabling CloudTrail. Amazon OpenSearch or Athena queries the archive. Lifecycle policies manage retention and cost.

blocks.text: Incident response without centralized logs is guesswork. Interviewers ask "how do you detect who deleted prod RDS?" Answer: org CloudTrail in immutable log-archive with SCP protection.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: org CloudTrail to log-archive S3, SCP prevents disable, Flow Logs + Config centralized, Athena/OpenSearch query.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Enable org CloudTrail
items.body: All regions, log file validation, KMS encryption, S3 in log-archive.

items.title: SCP protect logging
items.body: Deny cloudtrail:StopLogging and s3:DeleteObject on archive bucket.

items.title: Aggregate Flow Logs and Config
items.body: StackSet deploys to all accounts; central Kinesis Firehose optional.

items.title: Query and retain
items.body: Athena for ad-hoc; OpenSearch for SIEM; lifecycle to Glacier.

diagram.title: Log aggregation
diagram.source:
flowchart LR

snippet.label: Org CloudTrail
snippet.code:
OrgTrail:
  Type: AWS::CloudTrail::Trail
  Properties:
    IsOrganizationTrail: true
    IsMultiRegionTrail: true
    EnableLogFileValidation: true
    S3BucketName: org-cloudtrail-archive
    KMSKeyId: !Ref TrailKey
snippet.explanation: Single trail for all org accounts — landing zone baseline.

snippet.label: SCP protect trail
snippet.explanation: Member accounts cannot disable audit or delete archive objects.

snippet.label: Athena — who deleted ENI
snippet.code:
SELECT eventtime, useridentity.arn, eventsource, eventname
FROM cloudtrail_db.org_trail
WHERE eventname = 'DeleteNetworkInterface'
  AND date = current_date
ORDER BY eventtime DESC;
snippet.explanation: Incident response query — proves centralized logging value.

snippet.label: S3 Object Lock
snippet.code:
ArchiveBucket:
  Type: AWS::S3::Bucket
  Properties:
    ObjectLockEnabled: true
    LifecycleConfiguration:
      Rules:
        - Id: glacier-after-90d
          Status: Enabled
          Transitions:
            - StorageClass: GLACIER
              TransitionInDays: 90
snippet.explanation: Immutable retention for compliance; lifecycle controls cost.

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: CloudTrail only in management account, not org-wide. Logs in same account as workload — attacker deletes trail. No log file validation enabled.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: 100% accounts in org trail; SCP simulator confirms trail protection; mean time to answer "who did X" < 15 min via Athena.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Per-account CloudTrail with no central aggregation — rejected. Strong answer: org trail, log-archive account, SCP, Object Lock.

interviewTakeaways: Org CloudTrail to log-archive S3 — baseline for all landing zones.
SCP prevents disabling trail or deleting archive.
60s: Org trail all regions, central S3 with KMS and Object Lock, SCP protect, Flow Logs aggregate, Athena for IR.
Follow-up: how long retain CloudTrail for SOC2?
commonPitfalls: Workload account owns its only CloudTrail — attacker deletes it.
Strong answer: org trail, immutable archive, SCP deny stop/delete.
No log file validation — tampering undetected.
Infinite retention without lifecycle — cost explosion.
